title: Pius V & Gregory XIII condemn ‘no sin venial by nature’
source_text: XVII. Verum quum haec sententia sub finem superioris saeculi, ab aliquot Theologis in Belgio teneretur, & publice assereretur, singulari Bulla cum multis aliis eorum assertionibus, damnata fuit, tanquam erronea, a Pontificibus Pio V. & Gregorio XIII. Qua in Bulla inter multos alios articulos hunc quoque damnant, Nullum est peccatum ex natura sua veniale, sed omne peccatum meretur poenam aeternam. Ut refert Bellarminus, lib. 1. de Amissione Gratiae, & statu peccati, cap. 10. parag. Confirmatur.
pass_a_gloss: But when this opinion toward the end of the previous century was held by some theologians in Belgium and publicly asserted, it was condemned as erroneous by a special Bull, together with many other of their assertions, by the Pontiffs Pius V and Gregory XIII. In which Bull, among many other articles, they also condemn this: There is no sin venial from its own nature, but every sin merits eternal punishment. As Bellarmine reports, book 1 On the Loss of Grace and the State of Sin, chapter 10, paragraph Confirmatur.
pass_b_english: Late-sixteenth-century Belgian denials that any sin is venial by nature were condemned under Pius V and Gregory XIII.
Bellarmine cites the Bull’s article: every sin merits eternal punishment—is rejected as erroneous.
